# Coherent Time evolution

The Time evolution page uses a ground-hyperfine secular density matrix
$\rho=\rho_{F_a}\oplus\rho_{F_b}$, initially $I/N_g$. Every $m,m'$ element
within either manifold is retained. Inter-manifold coherences at the ground
hyperfine frequency are excluded. This is distinct from the ACC page's steady
population calculation and linear RF response.

For species $a$, in angular-frequency units,

$$
\dot\rho_a=-i[H_{B,a}/\hbar+u(t)H_{LS,a}/\hbar,\rho_a]
+u(t)\sum_j\mathcal D[J_{a,j}]\rho_a
+R_{ER,a}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes I_2/2]-\rho_a)
+R_{u,a}(I\,\mathrm{Tr}\rho_a/N_a-\rho_a)
+R_{SE,a}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes\rho_{S,a}]-\rho_a)
+R_{a\leftarrow b}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes\rho_{S,b}]-\rho_a).
$$

Here $u(t)=1$ before pump turn-off and zero afterward,
$\mathcal D[J]\rho=J\rho J^\dagger-\{J^\dagger J,\rho\}/2$,
and $\mathcal P$ removes cross-hyperfine blocks. Nuclear and electron reductions
come from the coupled-to-uncoupled Clebsch–Gordan transformation. Electron
marginals are trace normalized; nuclear marginals retain the target trace.
Both species are evolved in a common lab-z basis, so electron spin transfer
does not depend on their independently selected display bases.

The static Hamiltonian is
$H_B/\hbar=2\pi(\mu_B/h)10^{-9}B_{\mathrm{nT}}\sum_F g_F P_F F_b P_F$,
with dimensionless spin operators, the field's laboratory axis $b$, and the
existing signed hyperfine $g_F$, including the nuclear contribution. Thus
$\dot{\langle F_y\rangle}=-\omega_F\langle F_z\rangle$ for a field along x.
The linear Zeeman approximation is retained; Breit–Rabi mixing is excluded.

## Optical elimination and normalization

Each incoming ground manifold $F_i$ and excited manifold $F_e$ has a signed
absorption matrix $A_{ei}=\sum_q\epsilon_q d_q$, using the existing Wigner
dipoles and laboratory Jones polarization. If $r$ is the existing intensity
rate scale and $V$ its complex, peak-normalized Voigt response,

$$
J_{F_o,F_e,F_i,q}=\sqrt{r\,\mathrm{Re}V_{ei}}\,D_{F_o,F_e,q}A_{ei},\qquad
H_{LS}/\hbar=\tfrac12\sum_{ei}r\,\mathrm{Im}V_{ei}A_{ei}^\dagger A_{ei}.
$$

Emission matrices are normalized over all outgoing ground states and emitted
polarizations: $\sum_{F_o,q}D^\dagger D=I_e$. Each emission matrix retains the
amplitudes of all excited m states in that manifold. Splitting it into
independent m-resolved jumps would erase spontaneous coherence transfer and
break rotation covariance. Different incoming/outgoing hyperfine manifolds
and different excited F manifolds have separate jumps. Excited-hyperfine
interference and explicit excited-state precession are omitted.

On collinear diagonal states the dissipative populations reproduce the existing
optical rate generator. The dispersive Hamiltonian uses the same factor and
sign as the Light shift page. All active pumps, including off-target tails,
contribute to this dynamics. Pump-off removes both optical terms. Magnetic
shifts and light shifts are not fed back into optical detunings.

The use of an excited-state-eliminated ground master equation follows the
general approach discussed by [Chang, Guo and Qin, Phys. Rev. A 99, 063411
(2019)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.99.063411). The specific Voigt weighting
and secular collective jumps above define this application's approximation.

## Bases, integration and detection

The page offers section CSV downloads. The complete export helper described
below remains available programmatically; its former bottom-page button is removed.

The Atomic moments and Probe signal scanning expanders default to closed and
use native `on_change="rerun"` tracking with independent per-species keys.
Their content is guarded by the container's `.open` state: chart creation,
section CSV preparation and widgets run only while open. Steady-state convergence
and spectral readout are inside the scan guard, so they do not run on initial
page load. Cached physical evolution remains shared. Persistent setting keys
preserve axes, moment choices and scan limits across hidden-widget cleanup;
expander visibility is session UI state outside the saved-condition format.

Each species has independent display axes for populations and moments. The
physical integration and probe remain in laboratory z. The Zeeman axis defines
the displayed populations and exported coherences; the moment axis defines
electron polarization and local alignment. Changing either only re-expresses
the cached density matrix, without repeating integration. Both are independent
of the field direction. The local
transverse frames remain cyclic: q=z uses (x,y,z), q=x uses (y,z,x), and q=y
uses (z,x,y). The output is $U_q^\dagger\rho_{lab}U_q$, with the corresponding
spin rotation. Hyperfine totals, laboratory orientation and probe signals are
invariant under this change of basis. Complete CSVs record both axes; population
and coherence columns use the Zeeman frame while moment columns use the moment
frame. Section CSV metadata identifies the relevant frame and both selections.

The moment readout contracts the complete output density matrix with operators
in that same basis. Laboratory orientation uses
$U_q^\dagger F_j U_q/\hbar$, $j=x,y,z$, and is independent of the chosen basis.
In local coordinates $(u,v,q)$, the transverse alignment operators are
$Q_{uv}=(F_uF_v+F_vF_u)/2$ and $Q_{uu}-Q_{vv}=F_u^2-F_v^2$.
Their expectation values are divided by $\hbar^2$ and retain coherences.
All manifold-resolved moments are per total atom, without division by manifold
population. CSVs identify u and v explicitly; the complete export includes
all calculated moments even when their graphs are hidden.

The displayed hyperfine polarization is the scalar
$\langle\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf I\rangle/\hbar^2$. Since $\mathbf F=\mathbf I+\mathbf S$
and $S=1/2$, its eigenvalue in a ground-F manifold is
$[F(F+1)-I(I+1)-3/4]/2$. Thus the full-ensemble expectation is
$(I/2)P(F_a)-[(I+1)/2]P(F_b)$. Within-F coherences do not contribute to this
scalar operator, which is proportional to the identity within each block.
It vanishes for $I/N_g$, lies between $-(I+1)/2$ and $I/2$, and is independent
of quantization axis. The complete CSV exports it as the dimensionless
`hyperfine_polarization` field, alongside the retained manifold totals.

Complex adaptive BDF integration runs separately on each side of the switch,
with relative tolerance $2\times10^{-10}$ and absolute tolerance $10^{-12}$.
The result checks trace, Hermiticity and eigenvalue positivity before correcting
only numerical roundoff. Samples are allocated approximately in proportion to
interval duration, include the switch once, and target 20 samples per cycle
through the fastest possible rank-$2F$ Larmor harmonic. At 20,001 output samples
the page explicitly warns of possible undersampling. This cap does not change
the adaptive internal integration steps. Very fast precession over long
intervals can require substantial computation.

The detector contracts the complete density matrix with the existing Mathur
tensor, $\langle\alpha_{ab}\rangle=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\alpha_{ab})$, then propagates
the Jones vector through the uniform cell. The probe contributes no Hamiltonian
or relaxation. The complete CSV includes real and imaginary parts of every
independent upper-triangular within-F coherence; populations provide the
diagonal and Hermiticity supplies the lower triangle. They use the selected
Zeeman display basis and are dimensionless probabilities per total atom.

## Pump-on steady-state probe scan

`physics/probe_scan.py` builds the same coupled coherent master equation in
laboratory z and starts from the same unpolarized state. Pumps remain on for
the entire convergence calculation. Autonomous BDF intervals double until two
consecutive intervals have a maximum state change below $10^{-9}$ and a small
stationary residual. For each species the residual tolerance is $10^{-10}$
times its smallest positive dissipative rate plus a floating-point allowance
of $100\epsilon$ times its fastest generator scale. The initial interval is
the inverse of the smallest positive dissipative rate. Integration uses the
transient tolerances; 30 intervals are allowed. A stationary initial state is
returned directly. Trace, Hermiticity and positivity are checked before readout.
Failure to converge is reported rather than labeling a transient state steady.
This convergence time is independent of the user event-sequence times.

`density_probe_spectrum` evaluates the existing all-hyperfine-channel complex
polarizability sweep. Its frequency coordinate is relative to the bare
fine-structure D-line center; pressure shifts remain in the transition centers.
For a fixed density matrix, the unit-coefficient scalar, vector and rank-2
operators are contracted once. Their frequency-dependent coefficients are
then combined into the transverse $2\times2$ polarizability at each detuning.
Time and frequency readout share exact Jones propagation and Stokes conversion.
The continuous weak probe does not enter the stationary master equation.

Each species scans 2001 equally spaced points over its saved bounds. Defaults
are ±7000 MHz; a native two-handle range slider allows ±15000 MHz with a
minimum 10 MHz span, enforced when the handles meet. It writes the existing
independent minimum/maximum settings without changing the saved format. Changing
the limits reuses the cached steady state. Probe line, direction, polarization
and path length are inherited; its fixed detuning/reference transition and the
display quantization axes do not constrain the frequency scan. CSVs contain
plotted signals and frequency-origin, probe/cell/pump and convergence metadata.

The scan header uses native columns for a left-side label, a half-width slider
and right-aligned section controls. Its help and download share one horizontal
row, in that order; time-domain section controls retain their vertical layout.
The slider's native label is collapsed while its accessible label is retained.

Settings format 2.4 and the v3 coherent model identifier are both required.
Earlier settings are rejected without migration, as requested by the user.
